newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Inflation is bright spot in murky Russia economy.
newsitem.headline: Inflation is bright spot in murky Russia economy.

text.p: Russian inflation slid to new year-on-year lows in September, but wage arrears rose steeply and industrial production shrank in an economy struggling to rake in taxes and pay workers on time.

The State Statistics Committee said consumer prices rose just 31.7 percent in the year to September, the lowest level since economic reforms got under way in January 1992 and down from 37.1 percent in August.
But September industrial production was 6.8 percent lower than a year earlier, dashing economists' hopes that a prolonged economic slump was about to come to an end.
Wage arrears rose 10 percent in September alone, hitting a total of over 40 trillion rubles ($9 billion). Arrears were 36 trillion rubles ($8.1 billion) in August.

Wage and tax arrears are two of the biggest problems facing the Russian economy and officials announced new plans to tackle the tax problem on Tuesday, threatening to sue six firms for bankruptcy unless they paid their tax bills within a week.
"We cannot allow our most profitable companies to break the laws of God and society," Pyotr Mostovoi, head of the state bankruptcy agency, told a news conference.
"The debts make fractions of a percent of these companies' turnovers and none of them can say it is incapable of paying."
President Boris Yeltsin last week announced the creation of an emergency commission to work out how to resolve the tax problem and bring in extra cash.
